status.description: Reads the answer. Every other status arrives as an error body carrying recovery.

tokens.description: Reads what the passages cost, in tokens.

total.description: Reads how many passages on the line hold a term, before the cut: more than came back means a narrower grep, a `kinds` filter or a larger `max_passages` reaches them.

id.description: Names the document, to cite it as sil's.

kind.description: Reads what the document is: a guide, a tutorial, an FAQ, a glossary …

title.description: Calls the document this when citing it.

author.description: Reads who wrote these words, quoted verbatim from a source sil read: cite them, never as sil's own. Absent, sil wrote them.

url.description: Reads where the author's text was read, to hand the buyer.

from.description: Reads the node the document is written for.

role.description: Reads what that node is: the root, a top, a domain, a shelf, a kind or a leaf.

heading.description: Reads the heading the passage sits under; absent, it has none.

part.description: Reads where the passage sits in its document, to read on from it.

of.description: Reads how many parts its document has.

matched.description: Reads which of the asked terms the passage holds. Empty: none — it fills the minimum from the nearest documents and answers no word of the ask.

text.description: Reads the passage whole, or cut where `truncated`.

truncated.description: Reads that the budget cut the passage short here.

passages.description: Reads sil's passages for the terms, best first: every term, then more terms, then the densest, the nearer node breaking a tie. Empty: nothing sil holds here answers; say so, never the open web.
